newsitem.title: UK: ENERGY MINISTER BATTLE NOT AGAINST U.S. OWNERSHIP OF BRITISH POWER COMPANIES.
newsitem.headline: ENERGY MINISTER BATTLE NOT AGAINST U.S. OWNERSHIP OF BRITISH POWER COMPANIES.

text.p: British Energy Minister John Battle said he is not against U.S. ownership of British power companies, The Observer newspaper reported on Sunday.

Asked if he was worried about the stranglehold U.S. companies have on the privatised regional electricity companies, Battle told the Observer, "I am more worried about ensuring there is a secure and diverse supply of energy in Britain. In principle, I am not opposed to foreign ownership."
His comments come as PacifiCorp of the U.S. said on Friday it was making a recommended bid of 3.7 billion pounds to acquire Britain's biggest electricity distributor The Energy Group.
The bid is the latest in a string of forays by U.S. companies into the British energy market.
Battle's comments were likely to reduce speculation in London that a Labour government will refer the bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, The Observer said.
On Friday regulator concerns kept Energy Group's shares at a discount to the offer price of 690 pence plus a 5.5 dividend. They ended at 645 pence.
The newspaper also reported that Entergy Corp, the U.S. power company that bought London Electricity earlier this year, was poised to shed a third of London's workforce.
"Company insiders have been informally told that up to 1,400 jobs are at risk," the newspaper reported.
London Electricity now has 4,300 staff, before privatisation it had more than 7,000, The Observer said.
London Electricity could not be reached for comment.
